definitions.explanation: The physical property of a material that allows it to return to its original shape after being stretched, compressed, or deformed.
The ability of a system, plan, or policy to adapt to changing circumstances. Used figuratively in business, policy, and organizational contexts.

examples.japanese: この{生地|きじ}は{弾力|だんりょく}がある。
{肌|はだ}の{弾力|だんりょく}を{保|たも}つためにスキンケアをしている。
examples.english: I do skincare to maintain the elasticity of my skin.

examples.japanese: この{餅|もち}は{弾力|だんりょく}があって{食|た}べごたえがある。
examples.english: This mochi has a nice springy texture and is satisfying to eat.

examples.japanese: {弾力|だんりょく}のある{運用|うんよう}が{求|もと}められる。
{状況|じょうきょう}に{応|おう}じて{弾力的|だんりょくてき}に{対応|たいおう}していく{方針|ほうしん}だ。
examples.english: The policy is to respond flexibly according to the situation.

notes:
USAGE:
{弾力|だんりょく} has both physical (sense 1) and figurative (sense 2) uses. In everyday conversation, it often describes the texture of food or skin. In formal and business contexts, {弾力的|だんりょくてき} (the na-adjective form) is frequently used to describe flexible policies or responses.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弾力|だんりょく}がある (to have elasticity/springiness)
- {弾力|だんりょく}を{失|うしな}う (to lose elasticity)
- {弾力的|だんりょくてき}な{運用|うんよう} (flexible management)
- {弾力的|だんりょくてき}に{対応|たいおう}する (to respond flexibly)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {弾力|だんりょく}: elasticity (physical bounce; figurative flexibility)
- {柔軟性|じゅうなんせい}: flexibility, suppleness (broader concept)
- {伸縮性|しんしゅくせい}: stretchability (specific to materials that stretch)
- {弾性|だんせい}: elasticity (technical/physics term)
